events.what: Li and Yang claim an improved upper exponent θ≈0.314483 for Δ(x), beating Huxley's 131/416
Sourmelidis improves Soundararajan's 2003 Ω-result for Δ(x) via the resonance method
Mahatab independently improves Soundararajan's Ω-result for Δ(x) via the resonance method (Ramanujan Journal 2026)
Lamzouri obtains a conjecturally sharp Ω+ result for Δ(x), first improvement on Hafner's 1981 bound

judgement.doubts: The bullet asks about bounding Δ(x); the question stays open, so Ω-improvements are bounds, not a settled case. All three post-snapshot Ω events are in the same progress tier and all have ai_role none; the recorded event (Sourmelidis) is kept. The bullet's 'k = 1' is Wikipedia's indexing quirk (classical case is usually k=2); it does not change the reading. Li-Yang's pre-snapshot upper bound is also only a bound, so it could never have made this open_stale.

corrections.why: F3: the record's own summary says the three papers 'moved the bound' on Ω for Δ(x); improving an Ω-bound moves a quantity on a question that stays open, which is scope `bound` (progress), not a settled case (partial).
F14: a progress row settles nothing and carries direction null.
